name: China Manufacturing Scale
narrative: IFR reports that factories in China installed about 354,000 industrial robots in 2025, or 59% of global annual installations; the United States installed almost 38,500. These industrial-robot figures cover a broader category than humanoids. IFR reports Chinese suppliers accounted for 55% of China’s domestic industrial-robot installations.

key_metrics.name: China share of global industrial installations

recommended_actions: Manufacturing capex incentives stacking with bonus depreciation
Federal procurement preference for US-made systems (HR 8189)
Supply-chain support for actuators, batteries, lidar where China dominates upstream
Visa pathway expansion for robotics talent

name: Robotics Foundation Models
narrative: Robotics foundation-model developers aim to use shared models across tasks and bodies. Skild AI announced a $1.4 billion Series C at a valuation above $14 billion in January 2026 and introduced S1 in August. Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 research describes tests of mobile manipulation in homes outside its training set. Company demonstrations and reported results do not establish performance across all workplaces.

key_metrics.name: Skild AI valuation at Series C

narrative_sources.label: Skild AI — Series C and S1

recommended_actions: Compute access programs for academic + small-firm robotics ML (analogue of NAIRR)
Open-source model + dataset support via NSF
Light-touch on foundation-model regulation pending NIST AI RMF maturity

name: Humanoid Cost Trajectory
narrative: 1X began taking preorders for its NEO home robot in October 2025 at $20,000 for early-access ownership, with a separate $499 monthly subscription option. Unitree’s G1 was introduced at a $16,000 starting price in 2024. Prices, subscription terms, capabilities and service costs differ, so these offers do not measure total industrial deployment cost.
recommended_actions: Demand-side incentives via enacted bonus depreciation for qualifying equipment
Pilot-risk-sharing fund for first-of-its-kind robot deployments per RFA framework

name: Defense Robotics Procurement
narrative: The Department of Defense launched Replicator to accelerate fielding of autonomous systems. In May 2024 it said about $500 million was secured for FY2024 and requested a roughly equal amount for FY2025; the earlier goal of multiple thousands of systems was a fielding target, not a verified count here. Replicator 2 shifted attention to countering small uncrewed aerial systems. H.R. 8189 remains a tracked proposal.
recommended_actions: Sustain DIU + Replicator funding through next defense authorization
Pass HR 8189 to lock in domestic procurement for sensitive applications
Accelerate ITAR clarifications for dual-use robotics components

name: Industrial Humanoid Deployment Wave
narrative: Agility and GXO began a warehouse pilot in 2023 and signed a multi-year Robots-as-a-Service agreement in 2024. On October 26, 2026 they announced expansion to North Carolina and Tennessee sites, with deployments expected to begin in early 2027. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada signed a commercial agreement after a pilot in February 2026. Planned sites are not yet operating deployments.
recommended_actions: Pilot-risk-sharing fund — defray cost of first-of-its-kind deployments
Workforce co-investment to fund operator training alongside deployments
Safety standard clarification via NIST/OSHA for human-robot shared workspaces

name: Federal Policy Momentum
narrative: Federal policy includes research programs, proposed legislation and equipment restrictions. Treasury’s October 26, 2026 outbound-investment proposal includes embodied AI and laboratory robotics in defined technology categories; it is not a final rule. The FCC’s draft test-lab order is scheduled for consideration on October 29 and would apply to covered equipment authorization if adopted.
recommended_actions: Track HR 7334 markup schedule — likely a leading indicator of broader federal alignment
Track IRS guidance for eligible automation equipment under enacted Public Law 119-21
Track FCC conditional approvals and Commerce Section 232 investigation outcomes

name: Physical AI ("AI with a body")
narrative: Physical AI combines AI with sensing and action in physical environments. Skild AI introduced its S1 robotics foundation model in August 2026 and reports commercial customers; Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 research tests a mobile manipulator in previously unseen homes. These are developer-reported results, not independent evidence of general performance across workplaces.

narrative_sources.label: Skild AI — reported customers and revenue

recommended_actions: Treat robot foundation models as dual-use; track compute + data access alongside the AI Action Plan
Fund shared real-world robot data / sim infrastructure (NSF / NAIRR analogue) so value is not captured only by the best-capitalized labs
Watch foreign capital concentration in physical-AI startups for supply-chain + national-security exposure

name: US Robot Component Supply Chain
narrative: Robot manufacturing depends on components including motors, actuators, sensors and electronics. Westmag says its South San Francisco motor and actuator factory is ramping production and testing; this is a company-reported stage, not proof of output at scale. Commerce continues to list its Section 232 robotics and industrial-machinery import inquiry as an investigation, not a final robotics tariff.
recommended_actions: Extend NDAA Section 889 restrictions to robot actuators and servo motors sourced from adversary nations
Review potential Section 232 measures for precision gear reducers and brushless motors
Manufacturing capex tax credit (IRA-style) for US actuator and motor production
DoD Strategic & Critical Materials program should add servo motors and torque sensors to the monitored list
NIST / DoC supply-chain map of US robotic-component dependencies — public transparency on single points of failure
